Name: compression_erases_the_writer
Title: Compression Erases the Writer, Not the Gain: Abstraction Level of Transferred Experience Helps Only When Writer != Reader
Short Hypothesis: The benefit of compressing agent experience before transfer is an interaction with writer identity, not a main effect. For a reader consuming its own success-filtered pool, raw trajectories beat writer-compressed summaries and procedures at matched injected tokens; for a pool written by a different backbone the order reverses, because compression strips the writer-specific search, phrasing and binding content that only its author can imitate. The survey claim 'transferability rises with compression' (2604.15877) and the finding 'raw beats distilled skills' (2605.24117) are the two cells of one interaction: the sign of the raw-minus-compressed contrast is predicted by whether the writer is the reader, the writer's identity is undetectable at the procedure level, and stripping the writer's thoughts from raw traces moves self and foreign cells in opposite directions.
Related Work: 2604.15877 states the compression axis (memory -> skills -> rules) and asserts transferability rises with compression, with no experiment. 2605.24117 (SkillEvolBench) shows raw-trajectory reuse often beats distilled skills, but writer and reader are the same backbone and tokens are not matched. 2604.14004 (memory transfer learning, coding agents) finds high-level insights transfer and low-level traces cause negative transfer across domains, without naming model pairs, without a self-pool control and without token matching. 2605.12978 finds consolidated memories degrade relative to raw episodic ones, again same backbone. 2606.23127 (procedural memory benchmark, 382 enterprise tasks) reports that some skills transfer across backbones and others specialise, but does not manipulate abstraction level or compare against raw traces. 2608.07169 distils a teacher's trajectories into one hierarchical level for small students with no raw-trace or self-pool arm. Home literature: 2509.22230 (reasoning traces tailored to the student by filtering tokens improbable under it) gives the distributional-misalignment mechanism at training time; this proposal tests its in-context analogue. Archived abstraction_discards_bindings_and_repairs (5.95) varied abstraction within one writer; here the writer is the manipulated variable and the claim is that the contrast flips sign with it.
Abstract: Two published positions on how experience should be stored for reuse contradict each other: a survey argues that transferability rises with compression, while a benchmark finds that raw trajectories beat distilled skills because abstraction discards state-contingent cues. Neither manipulates who wrote the experience. We propose that both are right in different cells of one design. On ALFWorld we build three pools from the same training games -- expert walkthroughs, Qwen3-32B's own successes, and EXAONE-4.0-32B's own successes (collected at the same episode budget) -- and have each writer compress its own pool to three levels: raw trajectories, per-item summaries, and per-type procedures, each injected at about 420 tokens. Two 32B readers of different families read every level of every pool through one fixed retriever, so the self cells and the foreign cells differ only in writer identity at matched capability. The estimand is the interaction: (raw - compressed) for the reader's own pool minus (raw - compressed) for a foreign pool, with the retained-gain ratio per writer x reader x level, all net of a static expert-written procedure prompt and a memory-free baseline. Every confirmatory cell runs 674 games x 6 seeds, so two-cell contrasts have about +-3 net half-width and the interaction about +-4.2, and every margin is at least twice the half-width of its contrast. We predict raw wins in self cells by at least 6 net, compression wins in foreign cells by at least 6, an interaction of at least 8 net, that at the procedure level a reader cannot tell its own procedures from a stranger's (equivalence within +-6) and neither beats the static prompt, that re-compressing the foreign pool with the reader itself changes nothing (what matters is what compression removes, not who words it), and, as the mechanism test, that stripping the writer's thoughts from raw trajectories costs the reader's own pool more than it costs a stranger's pool. A null or reversed interaction, raw winning in a foreign cell, or thoughts that are equally dispensable for both writers falsifies the account and settles the survey's claim negatively for this domain.
Experiments: Domain and partition: ALFWorld. Bank = the 3,553 training games minus a held-out slice of 400 training games excluded from every pool; evaluation = 274 validation games (140 seen, 134 unseen) + the 400 held-out training games = 674 games per seed. Retriever fixed (Measurement A's); retrieval is deterministic per game, so every cell at a level sees the same retrieved game ids across seeds and cells. Writers: E = expert walkthroughs (1,465, minus held-out); Q = Qwen3-32B self pool (1,892 successes, minus held-out); X = EXAONE-4.0-32B self pool, collected on the same 3,553 training games at the same scaffold and temperature (about 3 GPU-hours), success-filtered. Levels, produced by the writer model itself from its own pool: L0 raw trajectory (k=3, about 430 tokens, as measured); L1 per-item summary (4-6 lines keeping object and receptacle names, about 70 tokens, k=6); L2 per-type procedure (one paragraph per task type distilled from the writer's own pool, all six injected, about 420 tokens). Compressor identity: writer-compressed versions (Q pool by Qwen3, X pool by EXAONE) are primary; the reader-compressed versions of the foreign pool (X pool by Qwen3 for the Qwen3 reader, Q pool by EXAONE for the EXAONE reader) at L1 and L2 form the compressor-identity arm. For E, which has no writer model, the compressor is the non-reader backbone so E stays fully foreign. Thought-stripped raw (L0s): the L0 items with thoughts removed, actions and observations kept including failed steps, template-normalised; at matched tokens k rises to about 5. Readers: Qwen3-32B and EXAONE-4.0-32B (family mismatch at approximately matched capability; both serving to be verified in vLLM before the first confirmatory cell). Cells per reader, primary at 6 seeds (674 x 6 = 4,044 episodes per cell): k=0; static expert six-procedure prompt (Measurement C); self L0, L1, L2; foreign L0, L1, L2 (writer-compressed); foreign L1 and L2 reader-compressed; self L0s; foreign L0s = 12 cells = 48,528 episodes. Secondary at 2 seeds (1,348 per cell): E L0; E L2 (non-reader-compressed); self L1 and foreign L1 at k=3 (k-matched); self L0 and foreign L0 from type-balanced pools = 6 cells = 8,088 episodes. Per reader 56,616 episodes; both readers 113,232 episodes. Throughput: about 18 episodes/min per replica, one replica per A100; each reader's cells run on their own GPU in parallel, about 52 h each; GPU1 first collects the X pool (3 h); compression is batched (each backbone compresses Q, X and E at L1 and L2: 12 short jobs, about 1-2 h total). Wall-clock about 2.5 days. Order on each GPU: the six headline cells (k=0, static, self L0, self L2, foreign L0, foreign L2) first, then the L1 cells, then the compressor-identity cells, then the stripped cells, then the secondary cells, so every confirmatory contrast is complete before any secondary cell starts; if EXAONE serves slower, GPU0 switches to a second EXAONE replica when the Qwen3 cells finish. Estimands: net gain over k=0 paired by game and seed; D(w,r,L) = gain(L0) - gain(L) for L in {L1, L2}; interaction I(r) = D(self) - D(foreign) at the pre-registered level; stripping interaction S(r) = [gain(self L0) - gain(self L0s)] - [gain(foreign L0) - gain(foreign L0s)]; retained-gain ratio per writer x reader x level with two denominators (the writer's own gain from the same pool, and the reader's self-pool gain at the same level), on gains over k=0, with cluster-bootstrap CIs, reported only where the denominator's CI excludes 0; everything also reported net of the static prompt. Manipulation checks (not predictions): token counts per level within +-10%; textual divergence between the two writers' L1 and L2 sets (embedding similarity and normalised edit distance per type) with a pre-registered rule: if the writers' L2 procedures are near-identical (normalised edit distance below 0.2 per type), L1 replaces L2 as the level of P1 and P3, and the first clause of P5 is reported as a manipulation-check outcome rather than a finding; per-type composition of each pool. Pre-registration of gates, margins, the level rule and the seed rule before the first confirmatory cell. Optional, outside the envelope above and only if the primary cells finish early: Qwen3-8B as a same-family lower-capability writer for the Qwen3 reader at L0 and L2 (2 cells at 2 seeds, about 1.5 GPU-h of collection), a descriptive capability-at-fixed-proximity arm.
Baselines and Ablations: Memory-free k=0 per reader (6 seeds). Static expert-written six-procedure prompt (Measurement C) per reader (6 seeds): every gain also reported net of it. Self-pool control at matched collection cost is built in (Q->Qwen3 and X->EXAONE, both from the same 3,553-game budget at the same scaffold and temperature). Compressor identity: foreign pool compressed by the writer vs by the reader at L1 and L2 (6 seeds; carries P4). Thought-stripped raw (L0s) for self and foreign pools at matched tokens (6 seeds; carries P6): separates the writer's phrasing from its actions and search. Expert pool E at L0 and L2 (2 seeds): a foreign writer with no search and no thoughts, descriptive. k-matched L1 (k=3) vs token-matched L1 (k=6, primary) for self and foreign (2 seeds). Type-balanced pools (equal per-type counts) for self and foreign L0 (2 seeds), because the self pools are type-skewed. Type-stratified (clean/heat/cool vs pick/look/pick-two) and seen vs unseen estimates reported for every primary contrast. Cut from the previous version to fit the envelope: the E re-compressed-by-reader cells, E L1, and the gpt-oss-120b writer arm; the optional Qwen3-8B writer replaces the latter as a cheaper capability-at-fixed-proximity arm.
Falsifiable Predictions: Planning noise (see Measurement): two-cell contrasts between 6-seed cells have 95% half-width about +-3 net; four-cell contrasts about +-4.2. Margins are fractions of Measurement A's +27 (6 = 0.22, 8 = 0.3) and each is at least twice the half-width of its contrast. P1 (self cells, raw wins): D(self, L2) = gain(raw) - gain(writer-written procedures) >= +6 net at matched tokens, separately in Q->Qwen3 and in X->EXAONE; D(self, L1) >= +6 likewise. Each of the four contrasts is scored on its own: falsified if its 95% CI includes 0 or its upper bound is below +6 (a null D(self) ~ 0 gives a CI of about [-3, +3] and falsifies). Produced by the self L0, L1, L2 cells at 6 seeds. P2 (foreign cells, compression wins): D(foreign, L1) <= -6 and D(foreign, L2) <= -6 net, separately in X->Qwen3 and in Q->EXAONE. Each of the four contrasts is scored on its own: falsified if its 95% CI includes 0 or its lower bound is above -6; raw foreign winning in any single cell falsifies that cell. Produced by the foreign L0, L1, L2 (writer-compressed) cells at 6 seeds. P3 (headline interaction): I(r) = D(self) - D(foreign) >= +8 net with a 95% CI excluding 0, for each reader, at the pre-registered level (L2, or L1 under the convergence rule). Falsified if the CI includes 0 or I(r) is negative for either reader; a null gives a CI of about [-4.2, +4.2]. Produced by the four cells self-L0, self-L2, foreign-L0, foreign-L2 for that reader. P4 (what is removed, not who words it): for each reader and each of L1, L2, gain(reader-compressed foreign) - gain(writer-compressed foreign) is zero within +-6. Confirmed only if the 95% CI lies inside [-6, +6] and includes 0; falsified if the 95% CI excludes 0 in either direction (reader wording helping or hurting; a true difference of 6 gives a CI of about [3, 9]); otherwise inconclusive and 4 seeds are added to the cells of that contrast. Produced by the compressor-identity cells against the writer-compressed foreign cells at 6 seeds. P5 (the writer is erased at L2): for each reader, gain(self L2) - gain(foreign L2) is zero within +-6 (confirmed only if the 95% CI lies inside [-6, +6] and includes 0), and neither L2 cell beats the static expert prompt. Falsified if self-L2 differs from foreign-L2 with a 95% CI excluding 0 in either direction, or if either L2 cell exceeds the static prompt with a 95% CI entirely above 0 (the rival account, writer identity as a main effect at every level, produces exactly this). Produced by the self L2, foreign L2 and static cells at 6 seeds. P6 (the removed content is the writer's search and phrasing): the stripping interaction S(r) = [gain(self L0) - gain(self L0s)] - [gain(foreign L0) - gain(foreign L0s)] >= +6 net with a 95% CI excluding 0 for each reader: removing thoughts costs the reader's own pool more than it costs the foreign pool, and the point prediction is that the foreign half is negative (stripped foreign beats raw foreign). Falsified if the CI of S(r) includes 0 or S(r) is negative (thoughts are filler or noise regardless of who wrote them). Produced by the self L0, self L0s, foreign L0, foreign L0s cells at 6 seeds. The retained-gain ratio is reported per writer x reader x level with bootstrap CIs as the estimand the brief requires; no prediction is stated on it because ratio(L2) > ratio(L0) is arithmetic on the cell means that already decide P1 and P2.
Measurement and Noise Control: Paired design: every cell runs the same 674 games with the same seeds, retriever and sampling settings as Measurement A; cells differ only in writer, level, compressor and reader. Planning noise scales the brief's +-8 net at 274 x 2 seeds (548 episodes) by 1/sqrt(episodes): a 6-seed cell (4,044 episodes) has per-cell net-gain half-width about +-2.9; a two-cell contrast (D, the P4 and P5 differences) about +-3; a four-cell contrast (I, S) about +-4.2; 2-seed secondary cells +-5.1. Every margin is at least twice the planning half-width of its contrast (6 vs 3; 8 vs 4.2), so the predicted outcome and the null give non-overlapping CIs. Seeds are fixed at 6 in advance, not escalated on demand; the pre-registered amendment is that if the bootstrap half-width of any primary contrast exceeds +-4 (two-cell) or +-5.5 (four-cell), 4 more seeds are added to every cell of that contrast before its point estimate is inspected. Mixed-effects logistic model with game random effects and cluster bootstrap over games (seeds nested in games) for all contrasts and ratios. Type-stratified estimates alongside. Injected token counts logged per episode and matched within +-10%; retrieval results logged so that every cell at a level sees the same retrieved game ids. Margins as fractions of the Gate-0 effect: Measurement A's +27 net is the reference; +6 is 0.22 of it, +8 is 0.3. Unseen-only claims carry the 134-game CI and are reported as secondary.

(2) closest named method, query 'cross-model transfer agent skills model-dependent negative transfer abstraction' --recent, channel s2+hf: 2608.22610 (coalition-aware skill reliability: cross-domain utility reversal), 2608.01149 PATH-Bench, 2606.03565, 2605.30723 (model-aware skill alignment), 2605.23899; none compares raw vs compressed by writer; id 2606.23127 verified with 's2cli.py paper' (382 enterprise tasks, 22 skills, transfer across roles and backbones). No collision found; the nearest, 2604.14004 and 2605.24117, occupy one cell each of the proposed interaction.
Risk Factors and Limitations: EXAONE-4.0-32B serving in vLLM is unverified; fallback is gpt-oss-120b as the second backbone (then family and capability are confounded and the claim is reported as foreign-writer only) or a second Qwen3-32B scaffold as a proximity-only foreign writer. P1 may fail (compression free even for the reader's own pool), which refutes 2605.24117 in this domain and is reportable, but then the interaction is a main effect of level and the title claim falls; P2 may fail (raw foreign wins), which settles the survey's claim negatively and also kills the title claim. P1 with P5 implies that the reader's own raw traces beat the expert static prompt, and P2 with P5 implies that a stranger's raw traces fall below it; both implications are exposed to the data in the same cells. L2 texts from different writers may converge, making L2 uninformative for the writer contrast; the convergence rule moves P1 and P3 to L1 and demotes the first clause of P5 to a manipulation check. The self pools are type-skewed towards easy types; the type-balanced ablation guards against a composition artefact. The thought-stripped arm changes k (about 5 at matched tokens); the stripping interaction S(r) cancels the k effect to first order, not exactly. ALFWorld procedures are short and the ceiling at k=3 is near 0.87 on unseen, so gains are bounded above; margins are set as fractions of the measured +27. Two 32B families approximate matched capability but their k=0 rates will differ; the retained-gain ratio uses each reader's own self-pool gain as one denominator to absorb this. Budget: 113k episodes at 18 episodes/min per replica is about 52 h per GPU; if measured throughput is lower the secondary cells are cut first, then the L1 cells of P1 (L2 stays), never the seeds of the headline cells. Capability at fixed proximity is only an optional descriptive arm (Qwen3-8B writer); the design manipulates proximity (family) at approximately fixed capability.
Addresses gap: G10 (compression-transferability claim untested against raw-beats-skills at matched inference cost), with G6 (same-backbone evaluation) as the manipulated variable.
Not a restatement of: Brief prior-result bullet Measurement A (expert raw k=3 gives +27/+32 net; unseen approx seen, procedure-bound): it measured one foreign writer at one level; this idea claims the sign of the raw-vs-compressed contrast depends on whether the writer is the reader, which no single-writer measurement can show. Digest card arxiv:2604.14004 (high-level insights transfer, low-level traces cause negative transfer): it reports a cross-domain main effect of abstraction with unnamed model pairs and no self-pool; this idea claims the low-level harm exists only for foreign-written traces and reverses into a benefit for the reader's own traces at matched tokens. Archived abstraction_discards_bindings_and_repairs (5.95) varied level within one writer; this idea fixes level and swaps the writer, and the interaction is the estimand.
Changes made: P1: margin raised from +4 to +6 and seeds raised from 2 to 6 on all self cells (two-cell half-width about +-3, so a null D ~ 0 now falsifies); falsifier restated as 'CI includes 0 or upper bound below +6', scored per cell and per level. P2: same seeds and margin (-6); falsifier made per cell and per level instead of conjunctive over both foreign cells; the L1 cells are in the 6-seed set. P3: unchanged as the headline, now at 6 seeds (half-width about +-4.2 against the +8 margin) with a fixed seed count instead of an on-demand escalation. P4: recast as a two-sided zero-within-+-6 test on the compressor-identity cells at 6 seeds; a reader-compressed version that is worse, not only better, now falsifies, and a wide CI no longer confirms; the E re-compressed cells were cut. P5: recast from a universal null into an equivalence test (self-L2 vs foreign-L2 zero within +-6, either direction falsifies) plus a per-cell falsifier against the static prompt (any L2 cell whose CI lies above 0 falsifies); this sharpens the claim: at L2 the reader cannot tell its own procedures from a stranger's. P6: the retained-gain-ratio prediction was removed as arithmetic on the P1/P2 cell means; the ratio stays as the reported estimand with bootstrap CIs and two denominators. It is replaced by a mechanism prediction with its own cells: the thought-stripping interaction S(r) (removing thoughts costs the self pool more than the foreign pool), which tests the stated mechanism, that what compression removes is the writer's search and phrasing and only its author can use it, rather than a consequence of P1 and P2. Budget arithmetic: 12 primary cells per reader at 674 games x 6 seeds = 48,528 episodes plus 6 secondary cells at 2 seeds = 8,088, so 56,616 per reader and 113,232 total; at 18 episodes/min per replica that is about 52 h per GPU with the two readers served in parallel, plus 3 GPU-h for the X pool and 1-2 h of compression, about 2.5 days wall-clock. Cut to fit: E L1, the E re-compressed cells, the gpt-oss-120b arm (replaced by an optional Qwen3-8B same-family writer at 2 cells, outside the envelope). The central claim was not softened: the sign flip of raw-minus-compressed with writer identity remains the headline, its margins went up (4 -> 6) rather than down, and two sharper falsifiable claims were added (P5: writer indistinguishable at L2; P6: thoughts are author-specific), each with a null that the design can reach and distinguish at the stated noise.
